transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I've been having some really unsettling experiences lately. I work as a teaching assistant, and... well, what scares me the most right now is that when I'm walking across campus, it just feels wrong. It's like I'm watching everything happen through a pane of glass. I feel like I'm not fully inside my own body, if that makes sense. And the buildings and the students walking past me... they just seem slightly unreal, like a movie set or something. It's really bothering me.
Have you been feeling consistently down, sad, or hopeless lately, or have you lost interest in activities you usually enjoy?

Well, I don't know if I'd call it sad or hopeless, exactly. It's more like... I just can't seem to feel anything good right now. 

Like, the other day, my husband cut some flowers from our garden and tried to make me tea. I knew it was a really kind thing for him to do, but I just couldn’t feel the warmth or pleasure I normally would. There was just this... blank heaviness instead. I just couldn't feel happy about it.
Do you find yourself feeling constantly worried or anxious about a wide range of different things in your daily life, such as your work, your health, or your finances?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not sitting around worrying about my finances or my health or anything like that. It's not a general worry about everyday things. It's just... I'm just dealing with this strange feeling of being disconnected from everything. But no, I wouldn't say I'm constantly anxious about a bunch of different things.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of detachment or this loss of pleasure in the past, perhaps months or years ago, or is this the first time you have ever felt this way?

No, this is the first time. I've never felt anything like this before. It just started recently, all these strange feelings of being detached and not being able to enjoy things. I've never had to deal with this in the past.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since these feelings began?

Um, no, not really. I haven't noticed any big changes with either of those. My appetite is pretty much the same as always—I'm still eating normally. And... I guess my sleep hasn't really changed either. I'm still getting about the same amount of rest at night. It's really just that detached feeling I mentioned, but my eating and sleeping seem fine.
Has there been any recent event or change in your life, such as a major stressor or a traumatic experience, around the time these feelings first started?

Yes, there was. Um, this has all been going on for six days now, ever since the lighting rig collapsed during the showcase. So, yeah, that was definitely a major thing that happened right around the time these feelings started.
Since the accident, have you been having any unwanted, vivid memories or nightmares about the lighting rig collapsing?

Yes, I have. It's... well, it's mostly during the day. The sound of the metal coming down just keeps barging into my head. I'll just be grading papers or making coffee, and then suddenly it's like I'm right back there. I can see the volunteer lying on the floor, and the students all pushing forward in a panic. It just flashes in front of me like it's happening all over again.
Since the accident, have you been going out of your way to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of the lighting rig collapsing?

Yeah, I have. I've actually been taking the long way around campus just so I don't have to walk past the atrium where it happened. And... well, if anyone even brings up the showcase, I just change the subject right away. If they keep talking about it, I'll usually just make an excuse and leave. I just don't want to talk about it or be anywhere near there.
